classification.difficultyReason: Use the two-unit guest scale and twenty-dollar subdivisions to read line points, calculate slope, then substitute a point to recover the intercept hidden by the truncated axes.

content.prompt:
A venue manager recorded the cost ($C$), in dollars, of hiring a function room for different numbers of guests ($g$) from 12 to 24.

The manager created a scatterplot and constructed a line of best fit to model the relationship between the number of guests and the cost.

spec.description: Guests and cost scatterplot with black circular markers, major grid, 20-dollar vertical subdivisions and the supplied line of best fit. Axes are truncated so the y-intercept is not shown.
spec.mathematics: Guest axis 10-30; cost axis 300-600 dollars. The line passes through the grid intersections (12,380) and (24,560), giving C=15g+200. Data point positions are chosen scatter values near the line.
spec.answerVisibility: The scatterplot and line are always visible. The derived gradient and equation appear only in answers.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}m&=\frac{560-380}{24-12}\\&=15\end{aligned}$$
The units of the gradient are dollars per guest.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Determine the equation of the line of best fit.
